_comment: Six complexions the shop offers, ordered light to dark: five re-toned and one that is the master as shot. Deliberately NOT strong - the audience is Tamil Nadu, so the ladder stays warm-neutral and lightly saturated instead of running to a deep golden/ebony contrast. skinL/skinS are exact targets measured on the frame's skin region in tone.py's units (skinL = mean of channels, skinS = highest minus lowest, 0-255). The five driven rungs share one saturation band (30-44) so no complexion looks airbrushed next to its neighbour; 'as-shot' carries the master's own measured numbers and is copied, never edited. 'fair' (190/24) was dropped on the shop's instruction: 6 cards, and the palest re-toned rung reads cooler and flatter than they wanted.

light-warm.desc: fair to light, soft warm beige, no orange

light-tan.desc: light tan, natural medium, the catalogue's base complexion

medium-brown.desc: warm medium brown, the most common shade in the market

as-shot.desc: the master itself - the model's own wheat-olive complexion, untouched

deep.desc: deep brown, still warm and clear, never muddy

ebony.desc: rich dark brown; the darkest the shop shows, stops short of charcoal

picker_order.why: decided by the shop owner 2026-09-06: the customer's own photo first, then light to dark. Nothing in the pipeline sorts by this key - the gates still use rank (lightness), so the neighbour-gap check stays physics, not merchandising.

_ladder_checks.note: light-warm 178 -> light-tan 164 -> medium-brown 148 -> as-shot 138 -> deep 130 -> ebony 114; as-shot is the source photo, so its lightness sits inside the ladder rather than at an end
